business_rules.statement: Multi-role users are allowed with additive permissions; permission combination is union, not intersection.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Policy decision point, step 3 of the resolution order

business_rules.statement: The audit log records the user identity and the action, never an 'acting as role' fiction.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Audit schema; no field accepts an actor-declared role
business_rules.applies_to: Every audited action on every surface

business_rules.statement: At least one Tenant Admin always exists; an approver role must exist whenever a Job exists.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Refusal at the moment of removal and at first-Job creation

business_rules.statement: Delegation is deferred beyond V1; cover is handled by manually adding and removing the role.
business_rules.enforcement_point: No delegation endpoint exists on any surface

business_rules.statement: Permissions across held roles combine as a union; no held role reduces another's permissions except through a platform-fixed prohibition.
A permission applies only within the scope of the grant that conferred it; scopes do not merge across grants.
Platform-fixed prohibitions refuse the action regardless of held roles, grants, scopes, tier, or account, including the root.
Every permission decision records which grant conferred the permission and at what scope.
The effective permissions viewer renders a status from the closed set for every action, with no blank cells.
While DEC-XROLE-001 is open, assigning a tenant role to an identity that holds a platform console role is refused, and the refusal names the open decision.
The implementation team's tenant-side capacity can author and submit and can never approve or release.
JBS holds no standing access by default; every JBS session is scoped, time-boxed, reason-linked, audited, and mirrored.
No surface renders a role selector, an 'acting as' control, an 'acting as' banner, or any session-level role context.
Every unavailable action renders with a reason from the closed status set; controls are not silently hidden.
A landing view changes only the first screen and confers no authority; every role may switch to any view within its scope.
No impersonation mechanism exists on any surface while DEC-IMPERSONATE-001 is open.
The Author of a submission cannot review or release it, on any surface, at any tier, under any role combination.
The Release Authority stage cannot be bypassed by any path, including Lane B publication of an unapproved change.
Lot release is Quality Manager only, uniformly, with no exception by work type, risk class, or tag.
No tenant configuration can widen any of these rules; a looser value is rejected outright rather than accepted and logged.
Where no second party exists, the platform holds the submission and states the reason; it never advances it.
No configuration on any surface produces an automatic approval on timeout, for any gate, item, proposal, or hold.
The absence of an approver never causes an approval; it causes escalation, then a controlled hold, then a safe stop.
A second-identity step-up authorises exactly one act and is released immediately afterwards.
A Severity 1 hold is released only by a Quality Manager's explicit decision, never by timeout, escalation, or agent action.
Removing the last Tenant Admin is refused, with the rule named, and no override exists on any surface.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Role removal path including support sessions

business_rules.statement: Creating the first Job in a tenant with no approver-capable role holder is refused with the same rule named.
Cached device permissions are honoured only within the offline credential-trust window and are then graded down per section 15.4.
An agent's effective permissions never exceed the intersection of enabled atoms, Studio-authored policy, and the platform-wide artificial-intelligence prohibitions.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Policy decision point on AI tool calls

business_rules.statement: No agent permission on any surface equals or exceeds any human role's approval authority.
Every cell of every matrix carries exactly one status token from the closed set; a blank, ellipsis, dash, or 'same as above' is a defect that fails acceptance.
The runtime policy decision point and the rendered Roles pane are generated from one configuration source.
No tenant role type can obtain any authenticated session against the Super Admin platform console under any configuration, including multi-role assignment.
Every denial writes an audit event carrying identity, attempted action, object, object state, and the failing test.
Deny by default. Never fail open. Never authorise from a cached decision whose configuration version is older than the last committed permission change for that identity.
An action that cannot be audited does not happen; the action and its audit event commit in the same transaction.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Transaction boundary in the owning service

business_rules.statement: Disabling or hiding a control never changes the authorisation outcome of the equivalent application programming interface call.
Every mutating route across all five surfaces is registered with the policy decision point; route-inventory coverage is 100 percent at release.
Every background job and every artificial-intelligence tool call executes under a named non-human identity whose permission set is a strict subset of the authorising human role.
A single sign-on assertion carrying a role claim not assigned in the Delivery Operations Hub grants nothing.
Queued captures uploaded after a permission revocation are preserved and quarantined, never accepted as official records and never discarded.
No account other than the Root Super Admin can create a console account or assign a console role, under any configuration.
The six enforced invariants present no off control to any account, and a direct application programming interface attempt to disable one denies and is audited.
An out-of-bound tenant configuration value fails the write and returns the bound; it is never accepted and logged.
No object in the platform create-read-update-archive matrix exposes a hard-delete verb to any role.
All twelve pending-capable privileged actions remain pending indefinitely without approval and never auto-apply.
Legal-hold release and compliance-emergency-path opening each require two distinct approving identities.
A severity-catalog change that would remove any element of the Severity 1 floor is rejected before it reaches the approval queue.
No console role can retrieve tenant record-level operational content outside an open, named access class.
Cross-tenant analytics return anonymised aggregates for every account including the Root Super Admin, with no configuration producing de-anonymised output.
Credential material is never returned by any application programming interface to any console role.
No account, including the Root Super Admin, can promote a capability that failed its evaluation scenarios.
An approved emergency pause never alters specification gate behaviour, severity classification, containment launch, or the Severity 1 hold on any device.
No console role can create a lot release, reassignment, qualification clearance, or version change command.
business_rules.applies_to: Four of the five command classes

business_rules.statement: No tenant role type obtains a session on the Super Admin platform console under any configuration.
The Read-only Auditor receives no Command Center session and no Command Center application programming interface response other than an audited denial.
Under hard suspension every surface denies writes except the enumerated completion pipeline.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Suspension state check, before role grant

business_rules.statement: Every module of all four tenant-facing surfaces carries a status for all five tenant role types, with no blank cells.
No role can override on-device detection, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold from any surface.
The inheritance rule: an unenumerated feature, sub-feature or function inherits its parent module cell status, narrowed by object state, prohibitions and scopes; it may never be broader.
Approval of a Job denies in draft, active, and archived, and succeeds in pending_approval only for a non-creator holding the approving role.
A capture arriving after a run record finishes never folds into the record; only the audited-recompute path applies.
A published workflow version cannot be edited in place by any role.
No tenant role other than the Quality Manager can release any hold, in any state, on any surface, under any configuration.
A tenant configuration attempting to remove any element of the Severity 1 floor fails the write with the floor stated.
Deterministic detection, severity classification, the Severity 1 hold, and the containment checklist all function with the device fully offline.
No surface displays an offline device's pending command as delivered, applied, or acknowledged.
No notification is the sole enforcement mechanism for any hold, gate, approval, suspension, or device command.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Enforcing controls independent of the notification track

business_rules.statement: In-app notifications cannot be muted by any role; only digest sections can be muted.
Acknowledgement never changes the business state of a hold, Job, clearance, or version adoption.
No tenant role can modify or delete a tenant audit event.
A partial audit result is never rendered as a complete one.
Every feature maps to at least one authorised role, or carries Client Decision Required with a DEC-* reference, or Not applicable with a stated reason for every role.
business_rules.applies_to: Every feature, sub-feature and function identifier

business_rules.statement: Every feature names every role explicitly prohibited from it as Explicitly prohibited, never left as an omission.
No widening by inheritance: a function's effective status may never exceed its parent sub-feature, feature, module or surface cell.
Floors are never inherited; any identifier touching a platform floor is enumerated explicitly.
Every Client Decision Required cell denies at runtime and names its decision identifier in the denial.

decisions.question: What do the Supervisor+ and QM+ forms mean across five additive, non-hierarchical tenant roles?
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint reads them as 'holders of this role, and holders of roles the matrix separately grants the action to', never as a hierarchy.
decisions.impact: Affects MTX-TEN-02c, MTX-TEN-08 substitute sign-off row, and whether a dual-role holder gains authority.

decisions.question: May one human identity hold both a platform console role and a tenant role?
options: (a) Prohibit coexistence on one identity; require separate accounts
(b) Permit coexistence with a mandatory cross-stream correlation view
decisions.adopted_working_position: Interim posture: prohibit coexistence, so the account-provisioning path refuses to add a tenant role to an identity holding a console role, with the decision identifier named in the refusal message.
decisions.impact: Tenant isolation, audit legibility, approval independence, implementation-staff mechanism.

decisions.question: Does an impersonation mechanism exist, given that Super Admin functions name 'impersonation control' but Part VIII defines no such feature?
options: Impersonation control exists as a Super Admin function
No impersonation mechanism exists; support sessions are read-only without exception
decisions.adopted_working_position: The interim build posture is that no impersonation mechanism exists.
decisions.impact: Determines whether any console route can render a tenant interface as another user.

decisions.question: Does Lane B auto-publication of an approved proposal bypass the three-stage Author, Reviewer, Release Authority chain?
options: No content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at each of the three stages
An approved Lane B proposal auto-publishes a patch version with no second approval, no ceremony
decisions.impact: Governs MTX-TEN-08 and MTX-TEN-09; whether the Release Authority can be bypassed.

decisions.question: What is the escalation default when no holder of the target role is on shift?
options: Escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.adopted_working_position: Escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift and mark the delivery visibly as a fallback so the gap is visible rather than silent (open drafting default).
decisions.impact: Affects MTX-TEN-15, MTX-TEN-19, FB-RBAC-14 and the no-substitute ladder.

decisions.question: How do the Studio authoring grant and the Agent Author capability reconcile with delegation being deferred beyond V1?
options: Model both as assignable capabilities administered by the Tenant Admin, with no person-to-person delegation
Implement person-to-person delegation for these two capabilities only, as a scoped exception
Defer the Agent Author capability itself to a later release
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation is option one: assignable capabilities, no delegation. Until decided, the build denies Supervisor access to the Agent Builder and names the decision.
decisions.impact: MOD-STU-15, MOD-STU-18, FEAT-TEN-AGENT-COMPOSE, MTX-TEN-13, MTX-TEN-17.

decisions.question: Does the Read-only Auditor have access to the Standards and Operations Studio?
options: Published content visible, drafts and in-review hidden
No Studio access with audit-log reconstruction only
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until decided, the build serves published Studio content to the Auditor and denies drafts and in-review versions.
decisions.impact: Every Read-only Auditor cell in MTX-TEN-02b, plus MTX-TEN-01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 09.

decisions.question: Which surface renders a Worker's own record and own certification alerts?
options: Hub read-only for the Worker's own record
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until decided, the build serves the own-record view on the Frontline Worker Application only and denies Hub access to the Worker role.
decisions.impact: Determines whether hourly floor workers need web accounts and browser access at all.

decisions.question: What is the Tenant Admin's Client Command Center presence beyond report-format authoring?
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until decided, read-only monitoring access is served and no operational action is granted.
decisions.impact: Eleven module cells in MTX-TEN-02c and the MTX-TEN-01 Command Center row.

decisions.question: May the Read-only Auditor role be combined with an acting role on one identity?
options: Allow it and rely on the audit log
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: prohibit, because independence is the entire purpose of the role.
decisions.impact: MTX-TEN-18; audit independence and the credibility of audit evidence.

decisions.question: Does a manual hold exist, and who may place it?
options: Quality-Manager-only manual hold reusing the existing release path and audit
Supervisor-requestable manual hold with Quality Manager confirmation
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: none at V1, because a manual hold carries no severity band, no containment checklist, and no defined release condition.
decisions.impact: MTX-TEN-10 manual hold row.

decisions.question: Who may perform a bulk export of worker personal data?
options: No bulk personal-data export at V1
Tenant-Admin-only with a mandatory reason and full audit
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: Tenant-Admin-only with a mandatory reason and full audit, since the tenant is the data controller for its own workforce.
decisions.impact: MTX-TEN-14 bulk personal-data export row.

decisions.question: May the Root Super Admin be both proposer and approver of a critical-class action?
options: Accept root self-approval as designed, documented as a residual risk
Require a second Admin authorisation for all root-proposed critical actions
Require a second authorisation only for a named subset (compliance suspension, device wipe, floor changes)
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: the third option, applying the two-authorisation model where the blast radius is largest.
decisions.impact: Ten critical-class action types plus two root-only administrative actions would be single-person acts.

decisions.question: May one identity hold two of the four platform console roles?
options: Allow it with identity-inequality enforced at approval
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: allow with identity inequality enforced at approval.
decisions.impact: An identity holding Admin and Platform Engineer could propose and approve, dissolving maker-checker.

decisions.question: Is disabling a console account root-only like creation, or an Admin action?
options: Admin-allowed with root approval after the fact
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: Admin-allowed with immediate root notification, since containment speed outweighs symmetry.
decisions.impact: MTX-PLAT-05 FUNC-SA-002 and MTX-PLAT-06 console account archive/disable.

decisions.question: Is granting JBS access an Admin routine action or a critical-class action?
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: Admin action for a new grant and critical class for an extension of an existing grant.
decisions.impact: MTX-PLAT-02 MOD-SA-16 and MTX-PLAT-13 JBS grant row.

decisions.question: How does custody of the single root account transfer between individuals within the client's organisation?
options: A documented backend custody-transfer procedure at the same level as commissioning
A second break-glass root credential held in escrow
Explicit acceptance of the single-custodian risk
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: a documented backend custody-transfer procedure, since a second root account would contradict the exactly-one rule.
decisions.impact: MTX-PLAT-13; operational continuity for twelve action classes with one approver.

decisions.question: Is the Prevention Agent's pre-authorised, Studio-authored policy a runtime human gate?
options: Pre-authorised policy with a runtime gate only for proposals beyond that policy
Action agents change state and every one routes through a human gate before any effect
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopted 2026-08-14: gating declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field — authoring-time policy for the Prevention Agent, runtime human gate for the Deviation and Containment Agent's proposals beyond pre-authorised containment, none — reasoning agent for every reasoning agent. failures_fallbacks.trigger: A permission-resolution defect grants an Area-scoped Supervisor authority across the Site because a tenant-scoped Quality Manager grant is also held.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Per-grant scope evaluation is a hard step and each permission is tagged with its granting scope, so the defect is detectable against the acting grant in the audit entry.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Actions have already been taken outside intended scope; they are not undone automatically.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected grants are revoked — instant server-side, eventual on devices — and the actions stand in the record with their true attribution.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The defect is fixed through the platform change-approval cycle; grants are re-issued with correct scopes.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: While DEC-XROLE-001 is open, an implementation permits console and tenant role coexistence by default because nobody prohibited it.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The account-provisioning path refuses to add a tenant role to an identity holding a console role, naming the decision identifier.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: An existing identity already holds both because it was created before the check existed.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The identity's tenant-side authority is suspended pending the decision, not its console authority; the tenant is informed through the mirrored audit stream.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The client resolves DEC-XROLE-001; identities are restructured accordingly.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A user cannot tell why an action is unavailable and assumes the platform is broken.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Every unavailable action renders with an explicit reason from the closed status set; the effective permissions viewer explains the full resolution path.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The reason is accurate but the user disagrees with it.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The action does not occur; the correct remedy is a role grant, not an interface change.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The Tenant Admin grants the role, subject to the segregation-of-duties checks.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant has exactly one authoring-grant holder, so no submission can ever reach a Reviewer.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Approval Queue states the condition plainly and names the Tenant Admin as the resolver. Nothing advances.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant has nobody else to grant the authoring grant to.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No Workflow is published; the floor continues on previously published versions. The platform does not lower the floor to accommodate a small tenant.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The tenant grants the authoring grant to a second person, or engages the implementation team's temporary capacity.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A Severity 1 hold requires release and no Quality Manager is reachable for an entire shift.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalation to on-shift holders, then the fallback tier, then the Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Nobody acknowledges; Critical re-notification fires at 4 hours, or 1 hour in Regulated-Industry mode.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The lot stays frozen. Production of that lot stops, the run parks, workers continue their other assigned runs, evidence is preserved in full.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Quality Manager acknowledges and decides; release rides the command channel and reaches devices at their next sync.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant approximates delegation by granting a covering role with a wider scope than needed.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The grant is permitted; the platform does not prevent a tenant from over-granting inside its own tenancy.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The over-granted person acts outside the intended boundary.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Platform-fixed prohibitions still hold; the over-grant cannot reach a specification-gate override, a run pause, a self-approval, platform authority, or an automatic approval.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The Tenant Admin narrows or revokes the grant.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant attempts to remove its last Tenant Admin during a reorganisation.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refusal with the rule named and a direct path to grant the role to another person first.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant genuinely has nobody else.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The account is not removed; the tenant retains an administrator on paper and is not locked out.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A new Tenant Admin is established platform-side under the change-approval discipline, and the departed one is removed in the ordinary way.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Policy decision point degradation: role configuration store unreachable, stale configuration, audit writer unavailable, or object-state lookup timeout.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-evaluate against the last-known-good configuration snapshot only where its version equals the latest committed permission-change version; any inequality is unknown and denied.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the audit writer is unavailable, no mutating action proceeds at all; read paths remain available.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Mutations denied platform-wide for the affected tenant; reads served; the Frontline application continues local execution, detection, classification and the Severity 1 hold.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Restore configuration reads, verify configuration version equality, re-enable mutating paths per tenant.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Matrix rendering and policy divergence: capability list stale, failing to load, or disagreeing with the service.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The interface renders the surface with all mutating controls disabled and a banner naming the degradation; it never renders controls optimistically.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the banner itself cannot render, the surface presents its read-only view with a persistent header stating authority could not be confirmed.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Read-only surface, mutations denied at the service, Frontline local loop unaffected.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Capability list reloads, version identifiers reconcile, controls re-enable.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Enforcement-path bypass: a new endpoint ships without authorisation middleware, a job runs under a borrowed identity, an upload is accepted without re-authorisation, or an AI tool call inherits the orchestrator's identity.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The runtime assertion denies the call and raises a bypass event.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where bypass events exceed a threshold, the affected route class is disabled for the tenant and the Tenant Admin is told which capability is unavailable.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Route class disabled; reads unaffected; the Frontline local loop unaffected.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The route is registered, the release is re-verified against the route inventory, and the route class re-enables.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Approval queue unavailability, or a critical request exceeding its re-notification interval twice.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Submissions fail closed with a stated reason; no change applies. An approval that commits without applying returns the request to pending with the partial state recorded.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the root is unavailable and critical requests age past their re-notification cycle, the platform escalates through its own notification machinery and requests remain pending.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Critical requests pending indefinitely with visible age; the platform continues on its existing configuration. They never auto-approve, never expire into approval, and never downgrade to engineering class.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Root approval or explicit return; queue health restored.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A privileged action applies centrally but its device-bound command cannot be delivered.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The platform never renders the action as complete; command states remain distinct and the console renders the true state per device.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device remains unreachable; propagation lag is recorded as telemetry.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The central record reflects the decision, the device reflects reality, and the difference is visible rather than hidden.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device reconnection; reconciliation is the acknowledgement writing back with per-device timestamps.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Access-class mirroring failure: the mirror write fails, the tenant's audit stream is unavailable, or the banner fails to render on a tenant surface.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Where the mirror write fails, the session does not open; an already-open session terminates immediately and the partial access is recorded on both sides with an explicit gap marker.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where neither mirroring nor banner rendering can be restored, no session may open; support work proceeds through layer-one telemetry only.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No platform access to tenant record-level content; layer-one telemetry available; the tenant's operations unaffected. Every layer-three access is blocked including the compliance-emergency path.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Restore the mirror path, verify with a synthetic session against a test tenant, re-enable.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Artificial-intelligence governance failure: an agent continues emitting after a pause, a disabled atom continues to be invoked, or an evaluation gate check errors.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Treat an errored evaluation check as a failure, never as a pass, and refuse promotion. The orchestrator refuses agent tool calls at the policy decision point.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Disable the agent's non-human identity entirely, which removes every tool path.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No agent activity, deterministic layer running, gates human-decidable.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Identity re-enabled after the resume approval; emitted activity timestamps compared against the pause approval timestamp.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A prohibition is enforced only in the user interface.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None — a failing prohibition test blocks release.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable; there is no degraded mode.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected capability is disabled entirely until the prohibition is enforced at the service.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Enforcement added, test passes; audit review of the interface-only period, with any successful prohibited action treated as a security incident.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Audit-writer unavailability.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Mutating actions fail closed; reads continue.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the failure persists beyond the 30-minute platform alert threshold, the console enters a read-only posture and the Admin issues single-tenant notices.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No unaudited change exists anywhere on the platform.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Audit writer restored; a synthetic audited write verifies; the outage is recorded with an explicit gap marker rather than a backfilled sequence.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The tenant enters a suspension state (soft, hard or compliance).
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Soft: master-data writes blocked, operations continue, banner to the Tenant Admin only. Hard: every surface read-only except the enumerated completion pipeline.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Compliance: all logins blocked immediately, in-flight runs stop, devices lock at next contact with the fixed message.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Local data preserved on every device; no data loss; no surface presenting a control the suspension forbids.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Soft clears on an explicit operator signal (DEC-SUSP-001 adopted position); hard is platform-initiated; compliance requires the dual-authorised emergency path.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The worker's role changes while the device is offline (stale capability list).
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The device honours its cached credential for the tenant-set offline credential-trust window, default approximately 24 hours with a 72-hour platform ceiling.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Past the window, the device requires re-authentication and offers no module beyond the honest sync indicator and the local queue state.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Work already committed locally is preserved; no new work starts.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection, re-authentication, command application in order; queued captures re-authorised and anything no longer authorised quarantines for Quality Manager disposition.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A function ships with no explicit matrix row and an ambiguous parent module cell.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: An unmapped action denies by default and raises a coverage defect.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The action is unavailable to every role until mapped.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The row is added and reviewed; audit review of any invocation before detection.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: State-transition race: two identities act on the same object as its state changes.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The losing write fails with the current state named, and the caller re-reads.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the object's state cannot be read, the action denies.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The object retains its last committed state; no partial transition exists.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The caller retries against the current state; no reconciliation required because no partial write occurred.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Release authority unavailable: a Severity 1 hold is in force and no Quality Manager is reachable.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalation routing resolves the Quality Manager role to the people on shift.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no holder is on shift, the default escalates to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery (DEC-NOSHIFT-001).
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The hold stays in force; production on the held lot stops. No fallback may bypass the Severity 1 hold and release rules.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Quality Manager acknowledges and decides; the hold's full timeline including the wait is in the audit log and the anomaly record.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Revocation that never reaches a device: the device does not return within the credential-trust window.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The cached credential expires and the device refuses new work, offering only the honest sync indicator and the local queue state.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device remains locked out of new work indefinitely; local data is preserved and encrypted.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No unauthorised new work, no data loss, no false claim of revocation having applied.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection, command application, re-authorisation of the queue, quarantine disposition by a Quality Manager. DEC-WIPE-001 remains unresolved for wipe commands.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Agent proposal without a decider: a Lane B proposal has no reachable Quality Manager.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The proposal remains open and visible.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: At 30 days it carries a stale flag.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Nothing changes; the configured value stands; no automatic adoption occurs, because Lane B never changes without a person.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Quality Manager decides; no reconciliation needed since no partial state exists.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Notification delivery failure: the email vendor rejects or the in-app channel fails.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The surviving channel carries the notification; the failed channel's state is recorded as failed rather than silently dropped.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where both channels fail, the notification remains created and queued and the escalation record shows unacknowledged; the enforcing control is unaffected.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The hold, gate, or suspension remains in force with nobody informed — safe but not acceptable, so the connectivity-loss protocol escalates at 30, 60 and 120 minutes.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Channel restored; queued notifications sent with their original creation timestamps preserved; any notification that never reached delivery is re-sent rather than expired.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Tenant audit read or export path fails.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reads served from the primary store without export while export capacity recovers.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The audit surface reports unavailability explicitly rather than rendering a partial list.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Writes continue under the one-transaction guarantee; reads deferred.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Read path restored; event counts compared against the write path for the window, equality being the passing result.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Coverage check unavailable: the identifier inventory cannot be extracted.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The release does not proceed. There is no degraded coverage mode.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The previous release remains deployed.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Extraction restored, check runs, defects resolved; the blocked release and its reason are audited.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An undecided authority reaching production: a Client Decision Required cell is implemented as permissive because a delivery deadline arrives before the decision.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The build denies the action and names the decision in the denial message.
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where a denial blocks a genuine operational need, the escalation is a decision request to the named owner, never a configuration change.
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The capability is unavailable and the reason is legible.
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The decision lands, the cell is updated, and the matrix and the runtime regenerate together.
